analysis.title: Nvidia's Nightmare From AI King To Historic Valuation Discount
key_insights: Nvidia's board is reportedly preparing to replace Jensen Huang. UBS points to the company's deep management bench. Leadership uncertainty adds risk alongside China exposure and Washington's demands.
NVDA fell another 7% in early Frankfurt trading and is almost 20% below its 200-day moving average. The last comparable undershoot was during Liberation Day, when it traded roughly 30% below.
Weekly RSI on the Frankfurt-listed NVDA chart is below the levels seen during the Liberation Day panic. The note says oversold does not mean the selling is over.
Goldman sees NVDA at 11x its CY27 EPS estimate of $16.70, with a Buy rating and $300 price target. It expects fundamentals to outpace consensus.
Before the latest selloff, NVDA had fallen to its cheapest valuation versus the S&P 500 in almost 25 years (Bloomberg/Authers).
Goldman's Q3 and Q4 EPS estimates are 6% above consensus. It projects Q3 revenue of $110B and Q4 revenue of nearly $125B, with better margins driving the upside.

Goldman forecasts FY2028 revenue of $718B. The debate is shifting to whether power availability and datacenter capacity can support the expansion. Goldman sees limited execution risk in 2027, with 2028 visibility the bigger uncertainty. Customer funding and AI monetization add complexity.
So far the broader market has held up relatively well, and investors are treating the Huang issue as an Nvidia problem rather than an AI problem.

Nvidia's share of Chinese data-center AI accelerator shipments fell to 34% in H1 2026, with Huawei at 28% (TS Lombard). TS Lombard argues US export restrictions are accelerating China's domestic AI ecosystem.
